title: C-reactive protein (CRP)
what: A blood test from a vein. It shows if there is inflammation in your body and how strong it is.
why: For fever, a suspected infection, joint pain, or to check how treatment works. High-sensitivity CRP is sometimes ordered to check the risk of heart disease.
duration: the blood draw takes 2 to 3 minutes; results usually in 1 day
tell_doctor: If you were recently ill, injured, or had surgery
Which medicines you take, especially hormones and anti-inflammatory medicines

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: The test is usually done in the morning on an empty stomach, or 3 to 4 hours after a light meal. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: No fatty food, alcohol, or hard workouts.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on a support
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with alcohol
Blood is taken into a tube with a needle
A cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: If you are scared or feel dizzy, say so. You can lie down
after: Keep the cotton pad pressed for 3 to 5 minutes
Your doctor will explain the result. The number alone is not a diagnosis

faq.q: What does a high CRP mean?
faq.a: It means there is inflammation in your body. The doctor looks for the cause. It may be a cold, an infection, or something else.

faq.q: How is CRP different from ESR?
faq.a: CRP rises faster and falls faster. That is why it is easier to track inflammation with it.

reminders.text: CRP blood test tomorrow. Have a light dinner, with no fatty food or alcohol.
